lead_independence.lead: Lee Olsen, general manager at Waldo's Restaurant and Bar, sent WPTV a video of the flooding on Ocean Drive after Wednesday's storm. He said it was among the worst he has seen. Olsen said he has been at the location for 20 years and Wednesday was probably one of the worst floodings he has seen. The water level was high. When Olsen walked out into the middle of the street, the water was up to his knees. Wednesday was not the first time this week the road flooded. The same thing happened on Monday.

article_framing_rejections.headline: New College of Florida spends nearly $1 million on outside PR consultants despite 13-member in-house team

lead_independence.headline: New College of Florida spends nearly $1 million on outside PR consultants despite 13-member in-house team
lead_independence.lead: New College of Florida has paid approximately $800,000 to two outside public relations consultants since 2023, both hired through no-bid contracts, even as the school maintains a 13-member in-house marketing and communications team, public records show. The spending comes as Governor Ron DeSantis has defended more than $60 million in state funding to transform the small liberal arts college of about 1,000 students away from what he calls woke indoctrination. More than $400,000 has gone to TMF Communications, run by Taryn Fenske, a former spokesperson for both New College President Richard Corcoran during his time as Florida's education commissioner and for Governor DeSantis. Fenske also led DeSantis' presidential super PAC before securing her no-bid contract with New College in July 2023. According to college invoices, Fenske has been paid upwards of $15,000 per month, plus travel expenses, to help improve the school's brand, create proactive messaging, and produce promotional videos.

lead_independence.headline: Vero Beach flooding on Ocean Drive threatens businesses as city says fix could cost millions
lead_independence.lead: Lee Olsen, general manager at Waldo's Restaurant and Bar, sent WPTV a video of the flooding on Ocean Drive after Wednesday's storm. Olsen has worked at the location for 20 years and said the flooding was probably one of the worst he has seen. When he walked out into the middle of the street, the water was up to his knees. Wednesday was not the first time this week the road flooded. The same thing happened on Monday.
